3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Lucian and I were waiting in my office ahead of our talk with the representatives of the Bludish movement.

4.speaker: Lucian Galade
4.text: "Forgive me, sir. As I wasn't involved in the preparation of this proposal, I wanted to make sure I didn't miss anything."

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Lucian was poring over the proposal Nia had prepared for the amendments to Article 6 and 7. She had completed it with extraordinary speed and with input from the Bludish rights movement.

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "How many times do you need to read that, Lucian?"

7.speaker: Player
7.text: "Lucian, are you okay? I thought you would have memorized the proposal within minutes of receiving it."

8.speaker: Player
8.text: "If there's something you want to say to me before the guests arrive, this would be the time."

10.speaker: Lucian Galade
10.text: "Of course I've read it, sir. But as I wasn't involved in its preparation, I wanted to make sure I didn't miss anything."

11.speaker: Lucian Galade
11.text: "Since you've already accepted their meeting, I don't think there's much to say until we hear what they bring up."

12.speaker: Lucian Galade
12.text: "Ms. Morgna did a fine job, but I'll be honest. This is too extreme to pass."

13.speaker: Lucian Galade
13.text: "Article 6 is modified with additional details on how to acquire or lose Sordish citizenship status. But the main change is the removal of the term 'Sord' -- which I must say is extremely significant."

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: He pointed to the first page of the proposal.

15.speaker: Lucian Galade
15.text: "Especially the line: 'Everyone who is bound to the Sordish state by citizenship is a Sord,' is modified to... "

16.speaker: Lucian Galade
16.text: "'Sordish citizenship' refers to all citizens of Sordland on the basis of equality regardless of language, race, color, gender, political thought, philosophical belief, religion or disability."

17.speaker: Lucian Galade
17.text: "It replaces the term 'Sord' with 'Sordish citizen', and clearly defines what that is. As much as it a good change in theory, I'm not sure if this is worth tanking the whole of our reforms."

18.speaker: Player
18.text: "I thought you would support me through this, Lucian."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Are you advising against changing our proposal?"

20.speaker: Player
20.text: "What do you mean? Are you showing me your nationalist side, Lucian?"

21.speaker: Player
21.text: "Well, don't stop there. Read the changes to Article 7 as well."

22.speaker: Lucian Galade
22.text: "Of course I will, sir. I'm just doing my job as your advisor. I don't see how anyone from the USP would be willing to support these changes."

23.speaker: Lucian Galade
23.text: "I'll be honest, sir. I don't see how anyone from the USP would be willing to support these changes."

31.speaker: Lucian Galade
31.text: "No, sir. I'm merely stating that I don't see how anyone from the USP would be willing to support these changes."

32.speaker: Player
32.text: "I want you to give this a chance, Lucian. I believe this is very important for the future, and I need your support."

33.speaker: Player
33.text: "The party doesn't support the current proposal anyway. At least we can shine a spotlight on Bludish rights with this."

34.speaker: Player
34.text: "I didn't get the full party's support for our current proposal, either... Honestly, I don't see why we should back off."
34.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Albin_Convinced"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Gloria_Convinced"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Albin_Convinced"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Gloria_Convinced"] == false)

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "You might be right. It was already difficult trying to get the party to back our initial draft."
35.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Albin_Convinced"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Gloria_Convinced"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Albin_Convinced"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Gloria_Convinced"] == false) == false)

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "With these additions, it will be nearly impossible."

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: He flipped to the second page of the proposal.

41.speaker: Lucian Galade
41.text: "The line in Article 7: 'Every Sord is equal before the law' is modified to..."

45.speaker: Lucian Galade
45.text: "'Everyone, regardless of language, race, color, gender, political thought, philosophical belief, religion or disability, is equal before the law'."

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: "What about you, sir? Are you really thinking of adding these to your proposal?"

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Not seriously, no. I just want to test the waters."

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "That really depends on how today's meeting goes."

50.speaker: Player
50.text: "Tell me straight, Lucian. What are our chances of passing this proposal?"

53.speaker: Lucian Galade
53.text: "I doubt Mr. Leke and Mr. Ejall can provide us with anything tangible that will change the minds of the majority."

54.speaker: Lucian Galade
54.text: "Unless something extraordinary happens, the addition of these changes would doom our proposal for failure. There's no question about it."

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: After I accepted the meeting, Nia informed us of their intention to convince us to add further changes to our constitutional amendment proposal.

56.speaker: Lucian Galade
56.text: "I can at least see how this change could have been workable, if it wasn't coupled with the first."

57.speaker: Lucian Galade
57.text: "My general advice is not to change the focus of our constitutional amendments by messing with these articles. Our priority should be reforming the governmental structure."

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: Livia stepped in and informed us that the representatives had arrived.

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: With my assent, she opened the door to let Mansoun Leke and Fetih Ejall inside.

60.speaker: Fetih Ejall
60.text: "It is great to finally meet with you, Mr. President."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "You don't seem too happy about this meeting."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Do you think they are here to ask us to change Articles 6 and 7?"

64.speaker: Player
64.text: "If there's something you want to tell me before the guests arrive, now would be the time."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: But since our statement with the PFJP, there were rumors that we would also include these changes in our proposal.

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: "Forgive me, sir. I just think we are in a precarious situation at the moment."

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: Lucian didn't seem too happy about my decision to put pressure on the Court by highlighting the discrimination in Article 6 and 7 of the Sordish Constitution.

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: "You already publicly criticized those articles for being discriminatory against the Bludish people. They'll expect you to act on your words now."

71.speaker: Lucian Galade
71.text: "But I advise against altering our proposal at the last minute. Especially with changes that would never be accepted by our party."

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: "With that said... If you don't act on this, you risk losing all the Bludish support you've gained so far."

73.speaker: Lucian Galade
73.text: "Sir. I believe your statement with Mr. Ricter put us in a precarious situation."

75.speaker: Player
75.text: "If we have the opportunity to change those articles as well, we have to seize it."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "Do you think there's no way to pass changes to Articles 6 and 7?"

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Don't worry. I don't intend to change our current proposal."

79.speaker: Lucian Galade
79.text: "It's true that Mr. Ersen's case gathered a lot of sympathy, even from the USP..."

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: "...But I must say it's not enough to pass the amendments. Not unless something extraordinary happens."

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: "As much as I'm troubled by the possibility of losing Bludish support, we cannot agree to change our proposal."

83.speaker: Lucian Galade
83.text: "My general advice is not to lose focus of our constitutional amendments by messing with these articles. Our priority should be reforming the governmental structure."

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: Livia stepped in and informed us that the representatives had arrived.

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: We shook hands and took our seats on the two sofas facing each other.

86.speaker: Lucian Galade
86.text: "Good morning, Mr. Ejall and Mr. Leke."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "It's good to see you, gentlemen. Please, have a seat."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "Good morning, Mr. Leke and Mr. Ejall. Why don't we take a seat?"

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "Barilbar zinjar, my Bludish brothers. Please have a seat."

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Mansoun and Fetih exchanged puzzled looks. Lucian raised an eyebrow.

93.speaker: Narrator
93.text: After a few seconds of awkward silence, we shook hands and took our seats on the two sofas facing each other.

94.speaker: Fetih Ejall
94.text: "You must know why we're here, Mr. President."

98.speaker: Fetih Ejall
98.text: "You know why we're here, Mr. President."

99.speaker: Fetih Ejall
99.text: "We must first thank you for pushing for changes to Article 6 and 7. This has been a lifelong quest of mine."

100.speaker: Mansoun Leke
100.text: "Thank you for your support of Mr. Ersen and the rights of Bludish people in Bergia."

101.speaker: Fetih Ejall
101.text: "First of all, we thank you for standing with Ishval Ersen and the rights of the Bludish people of Bergia."

102.speaker: Fetih Ejall
102.text: "But know this. If you're *really* willing to fight for the rights of the Bludish people, we will champion you to the end."

103.speaker: Fetih Ejall
103.text: "We never would have expected such statements of support coming from a USP president. You have our appreciation."
103.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Bergia_Governor_Bron"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Centralization"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true) == false)

104.speaker: Player
104.text: "I promise you, I am willing to fight for your rights until we achieve true equality between Sords and Bluds."

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "I think I've already shown you that my intentions are pure by involving you in our proposal."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "Why don't we jump straight to the point?"

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "That's great to know. Thank you, Mr. Ejall."

111.speaker: Mansoun Leke
111.text: "The addition of these changes to your proposal hasn't been announced yet, Mr. President. We hope to see you act on them."

116.speaker: Fetih Ejall
116.text: "I believe we made good headway with Ms. Morgna on the proposal."

117.speaker: Fetih Ejall
117.text: "Since it was your intention to start this process in the first place, I'd like to believe that you'll add these amendments to your reform package soon."

118.speaker: Fetih Ejall
118.text: "If we're already aligned and there's nothing to discuss about the proposal, we can immediately talk about how we can pass the changes."

119.speaker: Fetih Ejall
119.text: "With the support of Mr. Ricter and the PFJP, we have worked on a proposal to change the articles you singled out as discriminatory."

120.speaker: Fetih Ejall
120.text: "It was a bold move openly attacking the Sollist structure of this country, so I'd like to believe that we share the same sentiment about reforming our constitution."

121.speaker: Fetih Ejall
121.text: "If you're willing to listen, we can explain the details to you."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "As much as I support your cause, the timing of this may not be the best."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "I went over the changes already and I approve of them. Let's talk about how we can actually pass them."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "Before we discuss our strategy, I'd like to go over the changes together with you."

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "I'll be honest. It is still not guaranteed that we'll be adding these changes to our reform package."

128.speaker: Fetih Ejall
128.text: "Mr. Leke, could you read the proposed changes for us?"

129.speaker: Fetih Ejall
129.text: "Great. Mr. Leke, could you read the proposed changes?"

130.speaker: Mansoun Leke
130.text: "The ethnic term 'Sord' will be removed from the constitution. We will remove the lines that define the citizens of Sordland by nationality."

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: Mansoun took out a stack of papers and started reading.

132.speaker: Mansoun Leke
132.text: "Firstly, the line 'Everyone who is bound to the Sordish state by citizenship is a Sord' will be removed entirely from Article 6."

136.speaker: Lucian Galade
136.text: "And not only them. Do you really want to throw away your cooperation with the NFP?"

137.speaker: Lucian Galade
137.text: "I don't think we should lose the focus of our reforms."

138.speaker: Mansoun Leke
138.text: "As for the following lines in the rest of the article, the term 'Sord' will be replaced with 'citizen of Sordland'."

139.speaker: Mansoun Leke
139.text: "And the line in Article 7: 'Every Sord is equal before the law' will be modified to..."

140.speaker: Mansoun Leke
140.text: "'Everyone, regardless of language, race, color, gender, political thought, philosophical belief, religion or disability, is equal before the law'."

141.speaker: Player
141.text: "Gentlemen. I'm all with you on this."

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "These are very significant and necessary changes. But they should be the target of our next reforms. They don't have a place in our current reform package."

143.speaker: Player
143.text: "As much as I agree with these changes in principle, I don't have a sound plan to pass them in practice."

144.speaker: Player
144.text: "Are you crazy? This proposal will be crushed in an instant."

145.speaker: Fetih Ejall
145.text: "No. On the contrary, this is the perfect time."

146.speaker: Fetih Ejall
146.text: "Governor Bron's ultranationalist policies are now known all across Sordland thanks to Ishval Ersen. And the support from the presidency has given people hope."

147.speaker: Fetih Ejall
147.text: "Our polls show that the Workers Party will definitely make it to the Assembly in the next elections. Anybody can see the Old Guard is scared of us."

148.speaker: Mansoun Leke
148.text: "And with the public opinion behind your constitutional changes, now is the best opportunity to include the Bludish community in this."

149.speaker: Lucian Galade
149.text: "You might be correct about the sharp change in the public perspective, but I agree with President Rayne. The timing of this is not right."

150.speaker: Fetih Ejall
150.text: "Let us at least explain our proposal, Mr. Galade. Mr. President."

152.speaker: Lucian Galade
152.text: "Mr. President is right. Given the current political reality, adding these to our proposal would eliminate the possibility of any reform being made."

153.speaker: Lucian Galade
153.text: "If we can't reform the judiciary and the amendment procedures, what good does it do?"

154.speaker: Mansoun Leke
154.text: "If even the leadership of the governing party doesn't believe in the possibility of change, of course nobody else will."

155.speaker: Mansoun Leke
155.text: "But this is a fallacy. If you don't support us because of the existence of people who are against us, how do we even start fixing the problem?"

156.speaker: Lucian Galade
156.text: "I'm sure you understand. We need a realistic proposal. This is the opposite."

157.speaker: Fetih Ejall
157.text: "Ett'a. And that deadlock is what's created the liberation movement."

158.speaker: Mansoun Leke
158.text: "It's time this country stops pushing the Bludish people to the corners of society."

159.speaker: Player
159.text: "You sound like you're trying to justify the actions of the secessionists. I hope you're not referring to the BFF, Mr. Ejall."

161.speaker: Lucian Galade
161.text: "I must point out that given our current political reality, adding these to our proposal may eliminate the possibility of any reform being made."

162.speaker: Fetih Ejall
162.text: "You didn't hear our offer yet, Mr. President... Or do you have a problem with the proposal's contents?"

163.speaker: Player
163.text: "Okay, let's talk strategy. Let's hear your offer."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "Let's go over those contents one more time."

165.speaker: Fetih Ejall
165.text: "Sure. Mr. Leke, could you read the proposed changes?"

167.speaker: Fetih Ejall
167.text: "Exactly. As long as the government creates a deadlock and doesn't offer solutions, the Bludish people will have to do what it takes to defend themselves."

168.speaker: Fetih Ejall
168.text: "You know what I'm referring to, Mr. President."

169.speaker: Fetih Ejall
169.text: "As long as the government creates a deadlock and doesn't offer solutions, the Bludish people will have to do what it takes to defend themselves."

170.speaker: Fetih Ejall
170.text: "And as long as you label those people who fight for their rights as the villains, you are deepening the problem and turning it into a cycle of violence."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "Are you really trying to justify the actions of the BFF right now?"

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "So the only side at fault here is the government?"

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "I knew you were in cahoots with the terrorists."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "You are right. Many mistakes were made to the detriment of the Bludish people. We can't continue like this."

176.speaker: Fetih Ejall
176.text: "I'm not going to reply to that."

179.speaker: Fetih Ejall
179.text: "What I'm saying is that you can't ignore the background of how these movements came to be. Nothing appeared out of thin air."

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: "That does sound suspiciously like a defense of the BFF militants. Why are you refraining from using their name?"

181.speaker: Mansoun Leke
181.text: "You're not even listening, Mr. Galade. Are you looking for reasons to prosecute us too?"

183.speaker: Player
183.text: "They're right, Lucian. The Sordish state isn't entirely innocent."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: "I'm not looking for reasons, Mr. Leke. But if you give me one, you'll face justice like everyone else."

187.speaker: Fetih Ejall
187.text: "Fara!? Don't finish that sentence, Mr. President."

188.speaker: Fetih Ejall
188.text: "We will not sit here smiling if you're going to start throwing threats at us. Lok geduhe."

189.speaker: Fetih Ejall
189.text: "Gentlemen. Let's get one thing straight here."

190.speaker: Fetih Ejall
190.text: "Are you willing to support our rights? Or did you approach us for propaganda reasons?"

191.speaker: Player
191.text: "Since we're already on the same page, we should talk about how realistic it is to pass these changes instead."

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "But the Bludish movement must properly distance itself from the secessionists. Otherwise we will see no progress on these issues."

194.speaker: Fetih Ejall
194.text: "We will, Mr. President. If you give us your full support, we will."

195.speaker: Mansoun Leke
195.text: "Then let's talk about our offer and plan our moves."

196.speaker: Mansoun Leke
196.text: "Then why don't we talk about our offer and plan our moves?"

198.speaker: Player
198.text: "Yes, Mr. Ejall. I'm willing to support you."

199.speaker: Player
199.text: "I want to support this proposal, but you have to convince me that you have a sound plan to pass it."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "I thought we could find other common ground."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "No. I'm not willing to support your proposal."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "Stop throwing Bludish words around, Mr. Ejall. I hope for your sake that you didn't say anything bad."

206.speaker: Fetih Ejall
206.text: "I'm not going to indulge your power trip, Mr. Rejn!"

211.speaker: Fetih Ejall
211.text: "I don't see why I should stay if you're not willing to support us."

212.speaker: Player
212.text: "Look. I'm willing to support you, but I don't believe we can succeed."

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "Why don't we all just calm down and hear your plan?"

215.speaker: Fetih Ejall
215.text: "No, I didn't. I'm a *Blud*, after all."

216.speaker: Narrator
216.text: On his gesture, Mansoun also stood up.

217.speaker: Mansoun Leke
217.text: "Well... Nevertheless. Thank you for inviting us, Mr. President."

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: He sighed and shook my hand.

219.speaker: Mansoun Leke
219.text: "Please sit down, Mr. Ejall. Let's talk about our plans. I believe Mr. President can still change his mind."

221.speaker: Fetih Ejall
221.text: "I know you are rightfully wondering how we can gather a majority in both the Assembly and the Supreme Court."

222.speaker: Fetih Ejall
222.text: "If you can gather the support of the USP, the Assembly won't be a problem."

223.speaker: Lucian Galade
223.text: "The Bludish community was never excluded during the preparation process. However, the fact is that there is no major Bludish presence in the Assembly. And we can't simply bring a party that's not elected into the process."

224.speaker: Fetih Ejall
224.text: "In the past, Mr. Ricter and Ms. Suheil supported us greatly in this endeavor, and I believe the PFJP would get behind our proposed reforms."

228.speaker: Lucian Galade
228.text: "I hope you're aware that Mr. Ricter has already announced that the PFJP will not vote for our reforms."

229.speaker: Mansoun Leke
229.text: "Since Ms. Morgna's team involved us in the proposal, the PFJP leadership has been reaching out to us."

233.speaker: Fetih Ejall
233.text: "It's true. If you include our changes in your reforms, the tide can still be turned."

234.speaker: Mansoun Leke
234.text: "You've put them under a lot of pressure now. They've been campaigning for these changes themselves, and they are aware of the support they'd lose from the Bludish people if they vote no."

238.speaker: Mansoun Leke
238.text: "You've already made a statement together, denouncing Article 6 and 7."

239.speaker: Mansoun Leke
239.text: "This would put them under a lot of pressure. They've been campaigning for these changes themselves, and they are aware of the support they'd lose from the Bludish people if they vote no."

240.speaker: Mansoun Leke
240.text: "They've been campaigning for these changes themselves, and they are aware of the support they'd lose from the Bludish people if they vote no."

241.speaker: Mansoun Leke
241.text: "I think Mr. Ricter wouldn't risk that."

242.speaker: Lucian Galade
242.text: "Gathering the support of the USP is the real problem here."

243.speaker: Player
243.text: "I wouldn't count on the PFJP too much."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "Well, but that doesn't help me with convincing the USP."

246.speaker: Lucian Galade
246.text: "Do you think the conservative MPs will have a sudden change of heart?"

247.speaker: Fetih Ejall
247.text: "There is only one thing that can get them to work with us."

248.speaker: Fetih Ejall
248.text: "If Mr. Hawker and his puppets are looking to put an end to the liberation movement, I'm willing to cooperate with them and give them what they want."

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: Lucian's eyes widened for a second.

251.speaker: Fetih Ejall
251.text: "If you include these changes in your proposal, I will give you the best bargaining chip you can get. Intelligence about the BFF and the locations of its leaders."

252.speaker: Player
252.text: "Intriguing. So you really are a traitor to your cause."

254.speaker: Player
254.text: "How do we know the Old Guard will be convinced by that?"

255.speaker: Player
255.text: "Are you really admitting your direct ties to the BFF in front of the president?"

256.speaker: Mansoun Leke
256.text: "You're starting to show your true colors, Mr. Rayne."

257.speaker: Fetih Ejall
257.text: "Watch what you're saying, Mr. President. I came to you with respect, I demand the same."

260.speaker: Mansoun Leke
260.text: "This is what we offer because we believe in it. An end to the BFF."

261.speaker: Lucian Galade
261.text: "This would give us a significant edge, of course. But I still don't think it would be enough on its own. Besides, can you really deliver on your claims?"

265.speaker: Fetih Ejall
265.text: "I thought it was you who wanted to add this reform and invited us to talk."

266.speaker: Fetih Ejall
266.text: "We came here with a real offer and you keep questioning us. What's with this sudden change of attitude?"

267.speaker: Fetih Ejall
267.text: "I thought the administration was behind this reform."

268.speaker: Player
268.text: "If you can promise us the BFF, maybe we can make this work."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "You're forgetting something. We never promised you anything."

270.speaker: Player
270.text: "That's Lucian's personal opinion, Mr. Ejall. There is no sudden change. I am willing to support you."

271.speaker: Player
271.text: "I think this is too risky. I'm not willing to lose our progress by cooperating with you. No offense intended."

273.speaker: Player
273.text: "Be careful what you say in front of me, Mr. Ejall. You don't want to force me to start an investigation on you."

274.speaker: Mansoun Leke
274.text: "This isn't a joking matter, Mr. President."

275.speaker: Fetih Ejall
275.text: "So, what about our plan and offer?"

277.speaker: Fetih Ejall
277.text: "Then we can talk about the details."

278.speaker: Fetih Ejall
278.text: "So you don't intend to pursue these reforms at all?"

279.speaker: Player
279.text: "I want to. But I'm not convinced that your offer would make a difference. You have to give me more details."

281.speaker: Fetih Ejall
281.text: "There is nothing left to discuss here. We should take our leave."

285.speaker: Fetih Ejall
285.text: "As I said, I'm offering the Sollists an end to the BFF."

286.speaker: Fetih Ejall
286.text: "But to you, I'm offering the possibility to become the president who finished off the secessionists. The president who started a new age in Sordland."

287.speaker: Fetih Ejall
287.text: "Think of the popularity you'll enjoy. This would be a huge boost for the administration, and it will also help your standing with traditional Sollists."

288.speaker: Fetih Ejall
288.text: "And if we change the constitution in the process, the Bludish community will be applauding you with all their might."

289.speaker: Mansoun Leke
289.text: "If you have any questions, feel free to ask."

290.speaker: Player
290.text: "Tell me everything about the connection between the Workers' Party and the BFF, and why you are suddenly so keen on selling them out."

291.speaker: Player
291.text: "Tell me about the BFF. Are you certain your intelligence would help us catch all of their leadership in one go?"

292.speaker: Player
292.text: "If this becomes public, how do you expect to keep your leadership of the Workers Party?"

293.speaker: Fetih Ejall
293.text: "I will give you everything I know and can gather. Even the connections in my own party. I am prepared to do this for the greater good."

294.speaker: Player
294.text: "I'm all clear on your offer. Let's talk about how we deal with the votes."

295.speaker: Fetih Ejall
295.text: "As soon as you give the greenlight, I will suspend the people from our party who have ties to the liberation movement."

296.speaker: Fetih Ejall
296.text: "I am ready to give you the names of all of them when the time comes. If this achieves progress for Bludish rights, I am willing to go to the end."

297.speaker: Fetih Ejall
297.text: "Progress is progress. I think this would open so many doors for our people. And I don't hold the belief that the way forward is armed resistance."

298.speaker: Fetih Ejall
298.text: "Well, their claims go to ridiculous lengths. It's true that some of the founders had previous connections to the liberation movement, but most have abandoned it entirely."

299.speaker: Player
299.text: "So the party was always connected to the BFF, as the Sollists and the nationalists claim?"

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "Do you really believe the changes to Article 6 and 7 will go over that well with the Bludish community?"

302.speaker: Fetih Ejall
302.text: "The support for the Workers' Party is increasing more than ever. I firmly believe that we will make it to the Assembly in the next elections."

303.speaker: Fetih Ejall
303.text: "If we're to finally take place in the democratic process, I believe we must completely sever our ties with the liberation movement."

304.speaker: Fetih Ejall
304.text: "Our movement is now far larger than theirs, and we have to take this opportunity for the Workers' Party and for Bludish rights."

305.speaker: Fetih Ejall
305.text: "That's on your security forces, Mr. President."

306.speaker: Fetih Ejall
306.text: "But I'm very certain that the recent intel I received about their location is reliable. Among the leadership, the highest profile name is Awlan -- Dewlen Arge's brother."

307.speaker: Fetih Ejall
307.text: "What you do with that information is up to you."

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "Dewlen is already in Antel Rock. If we can get both brothers locked up, the BFF would be crippled."

309.speaker: Player
309.text: "Do you know who their current leader is?"

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "What else do you know about the BFF?"

312.speaker: Fetih Ejall
312.text: "Since the arrest of Dewlen Arge, I don't believe they have a single leadership position."

313.speaker: Fetih Ejall
313.text: "But his brother is the most respected high-ranking member inside."

314.speaker: Player
314.text: "What can you tell me about him?"

315.speaker: Fetih Ejall
315.text: "According to my sources, a group of four commanders are leading the movement in Sordland. Awlan Arge is among them."

316.speaker: Fetih Ejall
316.text: "I've learned that Awlan has been to Rumburg several times to meet with the Rumburgian Intelligence Directorate."

320.speaker: Fetih Ejall
320.text: "Apart from Rumburg, he also seems to have ties with the Golcondist administration in Derdia."

321.speaker: Fetih Ejall
321.text: "Since Operation Bear Trap commenced in Wehlen, rumors have been circulating that Awlan and his brigade are planning to increase their activity."

325.speaker: Fetih Ejall
325.text: "Since Operation Bear Trap commenced in Wehlen, Awlan and his brigade have apparently been cooperating very closely with the movement's Wehlen branch."

326.speaker: Fetih Ejall
326.text: "What's even more striking is a yet-to-be-confirmed report which points to the involvement of several wealthy Sordish businessman in smuggling Arcasian and Rumburgian weapons to them."

327.speaker: Player
327.text: "These are massive, Mr. Ejall. I want you to give all of this intelligence to my team as soon as possible."

328.speaker: Player
328.text: "This entire offer sounds too good to be true. I'm not sure if I'm willing to trust you."

331.speaker: Fetih Ejall
331.text: "I intend to give leadership back to Mansoun. The party still respects him immensely."

332.speaker: Fetih Ejall
332.text: "And his name hasn't been stained like most of ours. The government did not label him as a 'former terrorist', and neither was he declared a target by far-right nationalists. Yet."

333.speaker: Mansoun Leke
333.text: "As much as I feel like I'm not ready for that responsibility, I'm ready to do whatever it takes to grow the Bludish democratic movement. I'm ready to be the new target."

335.speaker: Lucian Galade
335.text: "I believe that according to their plan, that part is all on us, sir."

336.speaker: Fetih Ejall
336.text: "We'll give you the BFF and you'll get us the votes from the USP, Mr. President."

337.speaker: Player
337.text: "Just imagining talking to Gloria and Albin about the proposal again is giving me a headache."

339.speaker: Player
339.text: "I may convince the leaders of the party, but we may want to reach out directly to all 130 of our members."

340.speaker: Mansoun Leke
340.text: "Focus on the leadership and get your vice president to convince the MPs."

341.speaker: Mansoun Leke
341.text: "He has a way with words. I think he can sell this idea even to the staunchest conservatives."

342.speaker: Mansoun Leke
342.text: "I'm sure you can handle it, Mr. President."

343.speaker: Mansoun Leke
343.text: "What about it? You're already going directly against the Old Guard."

344.speaker: Mansoun Leke
344.text: "Don't you already have a plan to get your current reforms through the Court? What does it really change for you?"

345.speaker: Lucian Galade
345.text: "With all due respect, Mr. Leke, we are not children here. You know how risky this is. If we lose this, our entire reform package goes down the drain. Not just Article 6 and 7."

346.speaker: Lucian Galade
346.text: "The addition of these reforms would flip our plan upside down. The implications are not the same at all."

347.speaker: Player
347.text: "Really? Does Petr really have such an influence in the Assembly?"

348.speaker: Mansoun Leke
348.text: "Of course, Mr. President. He has a dialogue with everyone. He's able to reach all corners of the political spectrum."

349.speaker: Lucian Galade
349.text: "I'm sure Mr. Vectern would be helpful in getting votes, but I don't see how that would be enough. Besides, the Supreme Court is the main problem."

350.speaker: Narrator
350.text: He sighed and sat down again.

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "Then I'm sorry. I'm not willing to support your proposal."

355.speaker: Fetih Ejall
355.text: "This is a very dark time for the Bludish people in Bergia and we need all the help we can get."

356.speaker: Fetih Ejall
356.text: "Governor Bron's racist policies are being illegally protected by the Supreme Court under the guise of a large-scale threat by the so-called terrorists."

360.speaker: Player
360.text: "Don't worry. We are already working on a proposal to restructure the Special Zone. Governor Bron will soon be gone."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "Mr. Hawker is using Governor Bron to increase tensions in the country. If there really are terrorists out there, these two are where it starts."

362.speaker: Player
362.text: "As much as I'm against the Supreme Court's decision to delay the case, the BFF threat in the region is not some fantasy."

365.speaker: Fetih Ejall
365.text: "Ah, yes. We never would have expected such statements of support coming from a USP president. You have our appreciation."

366.speaker: Fetih Ejall
366.text: "It's great that we think alike on the matter."

367.speaker: Fetih Ejall
367.text: "I've heard about that. We ask that you prioritize it after your reforms."

368.speaker: Mansoun Leke
368.text: "Thank you for following up on this, Mr. President. I hope it becomes a reality soon."

370.speaker: Fetih Ejall
370.text: "I thought you were different, Mr. President. But you've proved my comrades right."

371.speaker: Fetih Ejall
371.text: "We'll never achieve anything tangible as long as the USP is in power. I'm certain of that now."

372.speaker: Fetih Ejall
372.text: "Then do your absolute best and make sure it doesn't fail."

373.speaker: Fetih Ejall
373.text: "We're not going to *negotiate* our rights here. Either you will fight for us and we will give you what I said in return, or you abandon the Bludish democratic movement."

374.speaker: Player
374.text: "I'm willing to fight for you. I will include these amendments in our reform proposal." [ADD NEW CHANGES TO PROPOSAL]

375.speaker: Player
375.text: "No need to be so dramatic, Mr. Ejall. Let's work together and finally change the Articles 6 and 7." [ADD NEW CHANGES TO PROPOSAL]

376.speaker: Player
376.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. Ejall, but I don't think I'm willing to take the risk. We can't lose a possibility to reform our constitution due to these two changes. We won't include them."

381.speaker: Fetih Ejall
381.text: "I'm not a Sordish politician, Mr. Rayne. You will see how serious I am about this."

383.speaker: Fetih Ejall
383.text: "Of course. As soon as you add the changes to Article 6 and 7 to your proposal."

385.speaker: Narrator
385.text: Manson was the spokesperson of the independents and the former leader of the WPB, while Fetih Ejall was the WPB's current leader.

386.speaker: Fetih Ejall
386.text: "You can threaten me all you like, Mr. President."

387.speaker: Fetih Ejall
387.text: "You know that nobody received more death threats than me in this country."

388.speaker: Fetih Ejall
388.text: "If you're not willing to support us, say it like a man."

390.speaker: Player
390.text: "Let's just calm down and talk about the offer."

395.speaker: Fetih Ejall
395.text: "You will find an ally in me."

396.speaker: Fetih Ejall
396.text: "And I will deliver my promises. You can count on what I said."

397.speaker: Player
397.text: "Thank you. Together we will achieve a better democracy in Sordland -- for everyone regardless of culture, language or ethnicity."

398.speaker: Player
398.text: "Thank you, Mr. Ejall. Together we will eliminate the BFF and set the Bludish people free from terror and division."

399.speaker: Player
399.text: "I hope so, Mr. Ejall. Your promises will be needed to convince the party."

400.speaker: Player
400.text: "This was a very productive and historic meeting, gentlemen. Thank you for coming here."

403.speaker: Narrator
403.text: They both stood up and shook my hand.

404.speaker: Narrator
404.text: This drastic addition to the proposal at the last minute would surely be a cause of contention.

405.speaker: Narrator
405.text: I had no idea whether Fetih Ejall's plan would work.

406.speaker: Narrator
406.text: They both stood up and left the office afterwards.

407.speaker: Narrator
407.text: I wondered if I could still maintain the support of the Bludish community after this meeting.
